items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: they played Fats Waller records all the time. That’s how I—

ctx.x: But jazz was part of the music. Jazz was part of the way the bands approached things. They were jazzed up and they were all influenced by jazz and I came in that way. I heard it and it attracted me and I loved the improvising and oddly enough I think people know when a soloist is making it, even if they have no idea what’s going on. There’s something that happens I guess, because look at all these people that show up at these festivals. I don’t think they have much of a clue, other than something strikes them.…

Yeah, I listened to the radio. We had no television set until 1949 or 50. Before that we were listening to the radio all the time. And in Detroit, they had, well actually the station was over across in Windsor, CKLW in Windsor, they played Fats Waller records all the time. That’s how I—
